Bob (Acme): hey team — seeing intermittent 401s while streaming from the hosted endpoint during a long SSE session. request-id: 01A9KZQY2H. Happens ~30–90s after connect. Token refresh in our app rotates the bearer token. Attached the curl I used to reproduce below, but figured you might want more precise reproducible steps.

Maria (support): thanks, Bob — can you confirm the full request-id (if multiple) and paste the exact curl you used (sanitized is fine). Also, did you include cookies or custom hmac headers? We usually ask for a minimal curl that reproduces the 401 and a trace (`--trace-ascii`).

Bob (Acme): full request-id from logs: 01A9KZQY2H-0001 and 01A9KZQY2H-0002 (second one after token rotate). here's the sanitized curl I used:

```
curl -N -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "User-Agent: Acme/1.2.3" \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-rlhf' \
  --compressed
```

We also set a session cookie from our proxy: `session=eyJ...` (we can strip it if you need). Output shows: HTTP/2 401 and then connection closes with chunked EOF.

Maria (support): okay — to triage we need: 1) raw curl with `--trace-ascii` so we can see handshake/headers, 2) a version that includes the cookie header if present, and 3) a curl that forces http1.1 and one that forces http2 to compare. Can you run these three short commands and paste the traces? Example we ask for: 

```
# http2 (default on many clients)
curl -N -v --trace-ascii curl_trace_http2.txt \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Cookie: session=<REDACTED_COOKIE>" \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-rlhf'

# force http1.1
curl -N -v --http1.1 --trace-ascii curl_trace_http1.txt \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Cookie: session=<REDACTED_COOKIE>" \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-rlhf'
```

Javier (eng): quick note — our auth gateway supports two signature modes if customers implement on-prem signing. We expect `X-RI-Signature: sha256=<hex>` (lowercase hex). If a client sends a base64 signature or `sha1`, you'll see an intermittent 401 on token refresh because the gateway validates token+cookie combos on reauthorize. If your proxy adds or rewrites cookies it can also break the signature calculation.

Try computing the HMAC the way our gateway expects and include it to reproduce:

```
# HMAC check (example)
echo -n "/v1/streams?model=redwood-rlhf\n" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "${SECRET}" -hex
# then put header: -H "X-RI-Signature: sha256=<hex-value>"
```

If you can supply the hex we can test against the gateway logs. Also include the exact path and body string you used to compute it.

Bob (Acme): okay will collect those traces. one question: our app rotates only the bearer token, not the cookie. Could that mismatch cause a 401 after rotate?

Sophia (oncall): yes — if the token is popped from the connection mid-stream and your proxy replays a cookie+old token on reauth handshake, the gateway can reject with 401 and close the stream. Also, some proxies terminate chunked transfers leading to an abrupt close; forcing keepalive and disabling proxy buffering often helps for SSE. Try `--no-buffer` on curl and see if behavior changes.

Maria (support): action items for you, Bob:
1) run the two `curl --trace-ascii` commands (http2 and http1.1) and `curl --no-buffer` variant.
2) if you use HMAC signing, compute the hex using the `openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac` command and include the header `X-RI-Signature: sha256=<hex>` in one run.
3) upload the three trace files + the raw app logs and the two request-ids as `debug-bundle-1758009999.tar.gz` to our secure upload link: https://support.redwood.ai/upload (please mark as private).

If you can provide the traces I (and Javier) will correlate with gateway logs and reply with a precise repro. ETA: we'll look in the next 2 hours once bundle is uploaded. :thumbsup:

Bob (Acme): thanks — uploading now, traces named curl_trace_http2.txt, curl_trace_http1.txt, curl_trace_nobuffer.txt. bundle uploaded to the link.

diag-bot: automated note — debug bundle 1758009999 received and queued for correlation. Reference: DBG-2026-00047.

Javier (eng): we got the bundle. early glance — I see a signature mismatch pattern (client sent base64 sig in `X-RI-Signature`) on the first request, and then on the rotate we see a cookie rewrite from the proxy that removed `Secure` flag. I'll run a deeper comparison and post the exact failing verification line from the gateway logs once I finish.

Maria (support): great progress. I'll follow up with a short postmortem snippet and recommended fix (compute hex-hmac and ensure proxy preserves cookie flags). If anything else shows up in logs I'll DM you directly. Thanks!
